# browser-automation-cli

> One-shot Chrome CDP automation CLI for AI agents with no daemon and no remote telemetry.

browser-automation-cli is a single-process Rust CLI that launches system Chrome or Chromium through CDP, executes agent browser actions, then finalizes and exits. Lifecycle: BORN, EXECUTE, FINALIZE, DIE. Product settings use CLI flags and XDG `config` commands only.

## Command Surface (v0.1.9)
- Full inventory (**71** names via `commands --json`, sorted): assert, attr, audio, back, batch-scrape, click-at, commands, completions, config, console, cookie, crawl, devtools3p, dialog, doctor, drag, emulate, eval, exec, extension, extract, feed, fill-form, find-paths, forward, goto, grab, heap, hover, image, keys, lighthouse, locale, man, map, mitm, monitor, net, page, parse, perf, pick, press, print-pdf, qr, record, reload, resize, run, schema, scrape, screencast, scroll, search, select-option, sg-rewrite, sg-scan, sheet-write, sitemap, storage, submit, text, type, upload, version, video, view, wait, webmcp, workflow, write
- Discovery: doctor (browsers_dir, lighthouse source, cache_redis, residual_disk + residual JSON), commands, schema (`schema <cmd>` or `schema --cmd`), version, locale, man, completions
- Global flags: **57** long flags in the global help, being **55** product flags plus `--help` and `--version`; source of truth is `browser-automation-cli --help`
- Config XDG: config init|path|show|get|set|unset|list-keys (`config unset <KEY>` restores a key to its built-in default; discover full keys via `config list-keys --json`)
- Stealth: ON by default; `--no-stealth` disables the anti-detection patches for this run; `--stealth-profile auto|chrome-linux|chrome-win|chrome-mac` picks the impersonated identity; `--stealth-seed <SEED>` pins the identity across processes, so an N-URL crawl in N one-shot processes does not present as N machines
- Proxy: `--proxy <URL>` (`http`, `https`, `socks5`) routes both Chrome and the HTTP engine; `--proxy-bypass <HOSTS>` lists the hosts that skip the proxy, in Chrome bypass-list syntax
- Human input: `--input-profile human|direct` (default `human`) interpolates pointer trajectories, applies dwell between press and release, and paces typing; `--input-seed <SEED>` seeds the input jitter for reproducibility
- Session shaping: `--warmup` and `--warmup-url <URL>` warm the session before the target URL; `--no-xvfb` skips the private virtual display on Linux
- Payload assertions: `--expect <EXPR>` asserts `key=value`, `key!=value`, or `key~substring`, repeatable and AND-conjoined; `--expect-exit-code` exits 65 when any `--expect` fails
- Navigate: goto (init-script, --handle-before-unload accept|dismiss), back, forward, reload (CDP Page.reload + ignoreCache)
- Scrape: scrape (multi-format --format/--formats; --engine http|browser; format/formats in run), batch-scrape, crawl, map, sitemap (map with --sitemap-only fixed on), feed (RSS/Atom/JSON Feed over the raw body, http engine), search (uddg clean), parse (PDF/DOCX/xlsx/ods, --redact-pii)
- Interact: view, press, write, type, keys, wait (multi --text OR; run url/url_contains/navigation/wait_timeout_ms), hover, drag, fill-form, select-option, pick (native select + HIG), submit, upload, click-at
- Observe: extract (--llm/--question/--schema-json), text, scroll (dy/dx in run), attr, assert, grab (png|jpeg|webp only; AVIF removed)
- Tabs/Dialogs: page, dialog accept|dismiss (`.data.dialog_settled`; multi-tab session_id isolation; --if-present), cookie, storage
- Capture/utils: console, net, print-pdf, monitor, qr, find-paths, sheet-write, sg-scan, sg-rewrite
- Network observability: `--capture-network` in the SAME process, then `net list` (--page-idx, --page-size, --resource-types, --include-preserved) and `net get <IDX>` (--request-path, --response-path)
- Local media one-shot (no Chrome): image info|convert|resize|download|exif, video info|download|convert|to-mp3|trim|thumbnail|manifest, audio info|download|convert|trim
- Advanced: eval, emulate, resize, perf, lighthouse (flag→XDG→PATH; unit fixtures incl. chrome-captured LHR 13.4.1; e2e mock SKIP), screencast, heap, extension, devtools3p, webmcp, mitm, workflow
- Multi-step: run (NDJSON or JSON array; --json full steps[]; --json-steps stream; partial data.steps on fail-fast), exec, record --url --path (--seconds default 30, --max-events default 200; writes replayable `run --script` NDJSON)
- Multi-step stdin: `run --script -` reads NDJSON steps from stdin, one step per line, against a single live session
- Stdin mode validates each line as it arrives (`validation: "per-line"`); EOF is the FINALIZE trigger
- Prefer stdin over shell process substitution: `run --script <(printf ...)` is rejected by the file jail
- Residual-zero disk (0.1.5 RES-01…12 still true): BORN auto-GC Singleton-only Chromium `/tmp` (60s floor); FINALIZE dual scavenge + re-scan; never kills host Flatpak Chrome
- Intentional residual: GAP-022 ~53 dups; GAP-023/024 PRD divergences
- Lifecycle: BORN, EXECUTE, FINALIZE, DIE; product law residual-zero process + disk

## Settings Contract
- Product settings: CLI flags + XDG via `config path|init|show|set|get|list-keys` only
- Important keys: dialog_settle_ms, chrome_path, lighthouse_path, openrouter_api_key, llm_*, cache_backend, cache_redis_url, lang, log_level, stealth, stealth_profile, stealth_seed, browser_mode, input_profile, proxy_url, proxy_bypass, proxy_username, proxy_password, http2_enabled, robots_user_agent, scrape_no_cache
- Complete reference: all **217** keys with default and purpose in [CONFIGURATION](https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/browser-automation-cli/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURATION.md); machine-readable via `config list-keys --json`
- Restore a default: `config unset <KEY>` is the inverse of `set`; `config set <key> ""` is NOT the inverse, because for a string key it stores an empty value the normal path never produces and for a numeric key it is a parse error
- Proxy credentials: `proxy_username` and `proxy_password` go in XDG ONLY, never in argv, because the process table exposes argv
- PRIVACY: [PRIVACY](https://github.com/danilo-aguiar-br/browser-automation-cli/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) states that no product environment variable is ever read
- Logging: `--verbose`/`--debug`/`-q` or `config set log_level` / `log_to_file`
- Color: `config set color true|false`
- Chrome / Lighthouse: shell path or `config set chrome_path|lighthouse_path` (lighthouse also flag)
- Dialog settle: `config set dialog_settle_ms`; read `.data.dialog_settled` after dialog accept|dismiss
- Cache Redis: `config set cache_backend redis` + `cache_redis_url` (`redis://` only; `rediss://` fail-closed)
- MITM globals: `--mitm`, `--mitm-ca-dir`, `--mitm-har`, `--mitm-hosts`, `--mitm-ws`, `--mitm-max-body-bytes`, `--mitm-no-media-bodies`, `--mitm-redact-secrets`
- `--mitm-ws` restates the default: WebSocket frames are always captured under `--mitm`, so passing it changes nothing
- Lang: `--lang pt-BR` or `config set lang` localizes suggestions
